raw_response:
Answer: A
Reason: Spontaneous pneumomediastinum due to alveolar rupture (Macklin effect) typically presents with mediastinal air in the absence of pulmonary consolidation or pleural effusion, whereas esophageal rupture (Boerhaave syndrome) is frequently associated with adjacent lung opacification, hydropneumothorax, or pleural effusion due to chemical mediastinitis and leakage of gastric contents.
